modules.name: Datum and CRS registry
modules.design_question: Which single horizontal frame and vertical datum let City LiDAR, HRDEM/MRDEM, SRTM, footprints and view-cone geodetic heights agree to centimetres where it matters?
modules.method: Canonical frame: horizontal EPSG:3157 (NAD83(CSRS) / UTM 10N, City LiDAR native); vertical orthometric CGVD28(GVRD), because City LiDAR 2018/2022 is CGVD28GVRD and BC legal surveys still use CGVD28 (LTSA 465C). Tag every layer with CRS, vertical datum, epoch and source edition. Convert CGVD2013 layers (HRDEM, MRDEM) to CGVD28 by inverting PROJ grid ca_nrc_HT2_2010v70_CGG2013a.tif (EPSG:10520, 0.05 m national accuracy), then measure and remove the residual offset against the City LiDAR DTM on flat open ground (median of hundreds of points). Convert EGM96 (SRTM) and EGM2008 (GLO-30) through PROJ grids and calibrate the same way. Never store ellipsoidal heights as elevations. Render each view in a local ENU frame: UTM grid scale 0.9996 shortens grid distances about 0.4 m/km and ignores curvature (about 70 m at 30 km). Confirm the Guidelines' geodetic datum with the City (views@vancouver.ca) before any compliance wording.
inputs: Public Views Guidelines s.2 'maximum geodetic height'
outputs: offset table City DTM vs HRDEM/MRDEM
one-paragraph datum statement for the app

parameters.name: Z_CGVD2013 vs Z_CGVD28
parameters.relationship: Z_2013 = Z_28 + delta(x,y), delta from HT2_2010v70 minus CGG2013a grid; CHS gauge offsets imply about +0.12 m at Vancouver (sign convention unverified).

parameters.name: Ellipsoidal vs orthometric
parameters.relationship: h_ellipsoidal = H_orthometric + N; N differs by model (CGG2013a, HTGVRDBC00, EGM96, EGM2008), so heights from different models must not be mixed.

parameters.name: UTM grid scale k
parameters.relationship: k is about 0.9996 at E=491 km; ground distance = grid distance / k, a 0.4 m/km shortening (12 m at 30 km). Computed.

parameters.name: Earth-curvature drop
parameters.relationship: drop = d^2/(2R) x (1 - k_ref); 70.6 m at 30 km, 61.5 m with refraction k_ref 0.13. Hand calculation.

parameters.name: MRDEM edition shift
parameters.relationship: MRDEM v1.1 changed the datum transformation, moving heights about 0.4 m on average versus v1.0; pin the edition and record it.

metrics.name: UTM tile-corner round trip
metrics.basis: City tile 490000_5459000 corners reproduce exactly with a transverse Mercator implementation (computed).

metrics.name: City DTM minus converted HRDEM DTM, open flat ground
metrics.good: absolute median at most 0.15 m, 95% spread at most 0.4 m
metrics.basis: City 2022 vertical 0.081 m (95%); EPSG shift 0.05 m; HRDEM 'generally better than 1 m'.

metrics.name: Layers carrying full datum tag
metrics.basis: Vista manifests state the model's vertical datum is unknown.

visualization: map of datum per layer with applied offsets
scatter of City DTM versus HRDEM DTM with offset line
modules.limits: PROJ holds national HT2_0; Metro Vancouver uses HTGVRDBC00, so local difference is unquantified. CGVD28 variants (CVD28BC, CVD28GVRD, CVD28GVRD2018) are not reconciled.
modules.human_judgment: Obtain the City's datum answer; approve the canonical datum and offset tolerance.

modules.name: Footprint authority and conflation
modules.design_question: Which polygon represents each downtown building today, including towers built after 2015 and separate podium and tower parts?
modules.method: 1) Load City 2015 footprints (154,124 polygons) and reproject to EPSG:3157. 2) Build a LiDAR building mask from City 2022 points (building-class returns with height above ground over 2.5 m), rasterise at 0.5 m, vectorise. 3) Match each City polygon to the mask by IoU: mask-only means new, polygon-only means demolished, IoU below 0.7 means changed. 4) For new or changed buildings adopt the LiDAR outline, regularised (simplify 0.25 to 0.5 m, snap near-right angles within 5 degrees). 5) Dissolve City parcel-split polygons when roof percentiles agree within 1 m so one tower is one object. 6) Use OSM (ODbL) only as a separate optional overlay for names and building:part hints; use Overture and City 2009 rows as cross-checks, not geometry sources. 7) Give every feature an id, fp_source, fp_year, lidar_date and change flag. 8) Hand-check roughly the 100 tallest towers against the 2022 orthophoto.
outputs: footprints in EPSG:3157 with provenance and change flags
list of new, demolished and changed buildings

parameters.name: IoU match threshold
parameters.relationship: Keep City polygon if IoU with LiDAR mask is at least 0.7; below that flag changed; mask-only features are new.

parameters.name: Mask height threshold
parameters.relationship: Building mask = building-class returns with z minus ground above 2.5 m (team choice).

parameters.name: Parcel-split merge
parameters.relationship: City splits contiguous buildings at parcel lines; dissolve touching polygons when absolute p90 roof difference is below 1 m.

parameters.name: Simplification tolerance
parameters.relationship: Douglas-Peucker 0.25 to 0.5 m bounds added horizontal error; 2018 LiDAR horizontal accuracy is 0.36 m (95%).

metrics.name: Footprint IoU versus LiDAR roof mask, towers 50 m and taller
metrics.good: 0.85 or higher
metrics.basis: Team threshold for outline agreement before extrusion.

metrics.name: Post-2015 towers present
metrics.good: all top-10 towers present with correct outline
metrics.basis: Wikipedia list shows Paradox 2016, One Burrard Place 2021, The Stack 2023, The Butterfly 2024, all after the 2015 footprints.

metrics.name: Footprint edge error versus roof edge
metrics.good: 0.5 m or less
metrics.basis: 2018 LiDAR horizontal accuracy 0.36 m (95%); City 2015 footprints stated as approximate.

visualization: footprint overlay on 2022 orthophoto coloured by source and change flag
modules.limits: LiDAR mask merges touching buildings and tree canopy; City 2015 outlines are approximate; construction after Sept 2022 is invisible. Overture's City of Vancouver source vintage is unknown.
modules.human_judgment: Decide whether OSM geometry is allowed (ODbL); hand-repair the tallest towers.

modules.name: LiDAR LOD1 height extraction
modules.design_question: How are robust roof and base heights derived per footprint and per tower part from 49 points per square metre LiDAR, including rooftop appurtenances?
modules.method: Per footprint, read City 2022 points inside the polygon shrunk 0.5 m (avoids wall and edge returns). Keep building-class first returns; drop noise and spikes (z more than 5 MAD from the 1 m cell median). Rasterise max, p95 and count at 0.5 m with PDAL writers.gdal (percentile output types p<n>), then take zonal statistics per footprint. Roof height = P_q(z) for q in 50, 75, 90, 95, 99 and max, following the six-percentile practice of 3D BAG (Dukai 2019). Ground = P10 of ground-class points in a 0.5 to 2 m ring, falling back to the DTM. Store absolute roof elevation in the canonical datum plus height above ground. Detect podium and tower parts by clustering roof z (Gaussian mixture or 1 m histogram peaks) and polygonise z-bands into LoD1.3 parts. Record n_roof, n_ground, RMSE per percentile, flat-roof flag, built-after-LiDAR flag. For view-cone tests use max and list minor rooftop items for human review under clause 3.1.2 (appurtenances count under 3.1.1); display with p90. Cross-check against published tower heights.
outputs: per-building roof percentiles, ground, parts, quality fields

parameters.name: Roof percentile q
parameters.relationship: h_roof(q) = P_q(z_roof) minus z_ground; store p50, p75, p90, p95, p99, max. Display p90; cone tests use max.

parameters.name: Ground reference
parameters.relationship: z_ground = P10 of ground points in a 0.5 to 2 m ring; 3D BAG uses percentiles 0 to 50 within a 0.5 m buffer.

parameters.name: Inner buffer
parameters.relationship: Shrink footprint 0.5 m before sampling roof points (team choice).

parameters.name: Minimum points
parameters.relationship: Require n_roof at least 100 and n_ground at least 20; mean density 49 points per square metre gives 49 per m2 of roof.

parameters.name: LOD1 RMSE benchmark
parameters.relationship: 3D BAG median RMSE to point cloud: 0.31 m flat roofs, 1.06 m non-flat; below 1 m for p75 to p99 on non-flat roofs.

metrics.name: Tower height error versus published
metrics.good: 1.0 m or less
metrics.basis: 3D BAG median RMSE 1.06 m; published heights may be to architectural top, so define the reference per building.

metrics.name: Block-to-point RMSE
metrics.good: at most 0.31 m flat, 1.06 m non-flat
metrics.basis: 3D BAG benchmark medians on Dutch buildings, not Vancouver towers.

metrics.name: Points per footprint
metrics.good: n_roof 100 or more and n_ground 20 or more
metrics.basis: City 2022 mean density about 49 points per m2.

visualization: roof z histogram per tower with percentile marks

libraries.role: LAZ decode for laspy (NRCan COPC files)

modules.name: Downtown ground surface and allowed-height interface
modules.design_question: What is bare-earth elevation Z_ground(x,y) in the cone datum, and how does it turn a cone's geodetic height into metres allowed above ground?
modules.method: Fetch only needed City 2022 tiles (13 tiles lie within 2 km of downtown; names are 1 km south-west corner UTM coordinates). Unzip LAS into a scratch folder outside the repo, read ground-class points with PDAL or laspy chunks, write a 1 m DTM (mean or IDW via writers.gdal) and a 1 m DSM (max). Fill voids by TIN interpolation under buildings and over water. Check against 2018 and 2013 LiDAR and HRDEM VILLE_VANCOUVER 2013 for gross errors. Convert to the canonical datum from M01. Publish a 2 m DTM or an error-bounded mesh (0.1 to 0.25 m) while keeping 1 m locally. Expose Z_ground(x,y) and the interface h_allow(x,y) = H_cone(x,y) minus Z_ground(x,y) for the height-limit surface module, with sigma_allow computed from LiDAR accuracy, datum calibration and cone-height uncertainty.

parameters.name: Allowed height above ground
parameters.relationship: h_allow(x,y) = H_cone minus Z_ground(x,y), both in one vertical datum; a ground error moves the limit one-for-one.

parameters.name: Error budget
parameters.relationship: sigma_allow = sqrt(sigma_cone^2 + sigma_ground^2 + sigma_datum^2); LiDAR 0.081 m (95%) is about 0.04 m at 1 sigma if Gaussian.

parameters.name: SRTM propagation
parameters.relationship: Delta h_allow = minus Delta Z_ground; SRTM actual vertical error about 10 m (16 m LE90 specification) gives a limit error of the same size.

parameters.name: Interpolation error
parameters.relationship: Linear interpolation error bound is (cell^2/8) x max second derivative; dense LiDAR keeps flat downtown error far below sensor noise.

metrics.name: DTM vertical error versus control
metrics.good: 0.1 m or less on open hard surface
metrics.basis: City sensor accuracy: 2022 is 0.081 m (95%), 2018 and 2013 are 0.18 m (95%).

metrics.name: Allowed-height uncertainty sigma_allow
metrics.good: 0.25 m or less
metrics.basis: Team tolerance; dominated by datum and cone-height uncertainty, not LiDAR noise.

metrics.name: Vista SRTM baseline terrain error
metrics.good: not applicable
metrics.bad: about 10 m typical, 16 m LE90 specification
metrics.basis: USGS statement on SRTM; Vista samples SRTM at 60 m with EGM96 heights.

visualization: difference map City DTM minus SRTM 60 m
modules.limits: Ground under buildings is interpolated. h_allow depends on the unconfirmed cone datum. The 2022 surface shows 2022 grade; later site works are absent. Bridges and viaducts need explicit treatment.
modules.human_judgment: Approve interpolation under buildings and treatment of bridges, fill and water.

modules.name: Multi-resolution terrain and North Shore backdrop
modules.design_question: How should terrain be tiered from 1 m downtown to 30 m mountains 20 to 50 km away while keeping skylines accurate and storage small?
modules.method: Rings from the study site: R0 0 to 1.5 km, City 2022 DTM at 1 m; R1 1.5 to 6 km, City LiDAR resampled to 2 to 5 m; R2 6 to 25 km, HRDEM BC-Lower_Mainland_2016-1m COG (bbox reaches 49.5125 N, about 25 km north of the Vista anchor) read by window and resampled to 10 m (DTM for ground, DSM for skyline); R3 25 to 50 km, MRDEM-30 DTM and DSM; beyond, GLO-30 or MRDEM overviews for skyline only. Convert all rings to the canonical datum via M01 and calibrate offsets on overlaps. Mesh each ring with Delatin or RTIN under a distance-scaled error epsilon(d) = tau x d x (HFOV/width); share boundary vertices or add skirts. Apply curvature and refraction at render time, or build views in a local ENU frame. Keep DTM and canopy (DSM minus DTM) separate so trees can be toggled. Compare skylines from sample origins with an HRDEM-based reference.
inputs: HRDEM project COGs and 1 m mosaic
outputs: ring meshes or int16 height tiles

parameters.name: Screen-space error limit
parameters.relationship: epsilon_max(d) = tau x d x HFOV/W; for 60 degrees over 1920 px (0.545 mrad per pixel) 1 px is 5.5 m at 10 km, 10.9 m at 20 km, 16.4 m at 30 km.

parameters.name: Slope-amplified horizontal error
parameters.relationship: Delta z = Delta xy x tan(slope); SRTM 20 m CE90 on a 30 degree slope gives about 11.5 m vertical error.

parameters.name: SRTM native cell
parameters.relationship: 1 arc-second is about 30.9 m north-south by 20.1 m east-west at 49.3 N; Vista samples at 60 m and 300 m (coarser than native).

parameters.name: Raster cell count
parameters.relationship: N = area / cell^2; a 20 x 15 km window is 3.0 million cells (6 MB int16) at 10 m but 75 million (150 MB) at 2 m.

parameters.name: Ring boundaries
parameters.relationship: R0 0 to 1.5 km at 1 m; R1 to 6 km at 2 to 5 m; R2 to 25 km at 10 m; R3 to 50 km at 30 m (team starting values).

metrics.name: Mesh error versus distance
metrics.good: at most 0.5 px equivalent (about 5 m at 20 km)
metrics.basis: Pixel angle from assumed 60 degree, 1920 px view; tune per camera.

metrics.name: Mountain DTM accuracy by source
metrics.good: HRDEM better than 1 m; MRDEM-30 DTM RMSE 1.04 m non-vegetated, 2.55 m vegetated versus RTK
metrics.bad: SRTM about 10 m; GLO-30 below 4 m LE90
metrics.basis: HRDEM spec s.7.5; MRDEM spec Table 2; USGS SRTM; Copernicus collection page.

metrics.name: Peak elevation sanity check
metrics.good: within 5 m of 1,449 m (Seymour) and 1,231 m (Grouse)
metrics.basis: Published peak heights are Wikipedia values with unstated datum; use as a coarse check only.

visualization: ring map with source and resolution
skyline silhouette overlay: HRDEM versus MRDEM versus SRTM
modules.limits: HRDEM S3 COGs are EPSG:3979, not UTM. HRDEM mosaics can show steps where LiDAR vintages join. DSM includes forest canopy. Wheels for Python 3.13 on Windows are unconfirmed for pydelatin.
modules.human_judgment: Choose DTM or DSM for skylines; set tau and ring radii; accept 30 m cells beyond 25 km.

modules.name: Compact storage and web delivery
modules.design_question: Which formats and tiling keep every layer inside GitHub Pages limits yet load quickly in the browser?
modules.method: Store buildings as quantised footprint rings plus attributes (id, base elevation, roof percentiles, parts, flags) rather than baked triangles; triangulate in the browser with earcut. Store terrain as per-ring quantised meshes or int16 height tiles with deflate/zstd, in tile folders (for example 1 km) with a manifest listing sha256, CRS, vertical datum, source edition and attribution, as Vista's release manifest already does. Keep raw LAS, COG windows and intermediate rasters outside the repository; commit only derived files well under 50 MiB (warning) and 100 MiB (block). Serve from GitHub Pages (site at most 1 GB) with lazy loading per tile; use release assets for large optional packs. Build reproducibly from a Python script that records tool and data versions. Benchmark against Vista's 52.0 MB bundle and 982 and 320 bytes per building.
inputs: footprints and heights from M02 and M03
terrain products from M04 and M05
outputs: tile folders with quantised buildings and terrain

parameters.name: Per-building bytes
parameters.relationship: About 4 x n_vertices + 8; n=10 gives 48 B; 154,124 City 2015 polygons would be about 7.4 MB raw before compression (computed estimate).

parameters.name: Vista building cost
parameters.relationship: Central model 9,722,568 B for 9,897 buildings is 982 B each; extension 16,473,300 B for 51,510 is 320 B each (full triangle meshes).

parameters.name: Vista terrain cost
parameters.relationship: Terrain 1,104,396 B for 41,336 triangles is 26.7 B per triangle; backdrop 435,492 B for 23,822 is 18.3 B per triangle.

parameters.name: GitHub limits
parameters.relationship: Pages site at most 1 GB; repo advised under 1 GB; warning at 50 MiB and block at 100 MiB per file; 100 GB per month soft bandwidth.

metrics.name: Initial-load bundle size
metrics.good: 25 MB or less
metrics.basis: Vista release totals 51,990,003 B across 60 files; team target halves it with tiling.

metrics.name: Largest single file
metrics.good: below 50 MiB
metrics.basis: GitHub warns at 50 MiB and blocks at 100 MiB.

metrics.name: Bytes per building
metrics.good: 100 B or less
metrics.basis: Vista currently 320 to 982 B per building.

modules.name: Accuracy audit versus Vista and published heights
modules.design_question: How far do LiDAR-derived heights and terrain differ from Vista's OSM and SRTM context, and do they reproduce published checks?
modules.method: Define a regression set: (a) about 40 downtown towers with published heights; (b) 20 or more UBC campus buildings with ubcv_Structures bldgheight (2021 LiDAR); (c) 200 random downtown buildings, LiDAR height versus Vista height; (d) 500 terrain points, Vista SRTM 60 m surface versus City DTM after datum calibration; (e) cone-flip analysis: for each protected view, count buildings whose cone-intersection status changes when OSM heights are replaced by LiDAR heights, using test H_cone values. Report median, p95 and maximum absolute error by tier, with maps and histograms. Run the numbers in CI on a small fixture tile (490000_5459000) so each change stays within tolerance. Publish the results beside the data as an accuracy statement. Vista baseline facts: central model 9,897 buildings with 1,441 measured OSM heights, 3,656 from levels and 4,800 estimated by type; extension 51,510 buildings from current OSM.

parameters.name: Vista measured-height share
parameters.relationship: 1,441 of 9,897 central buildings (14.6%) have OSM heights; 3,656 (36.9%) come from levels; 4,800 (48.5%) are estimated by type.

parameters.name: Vista terrain
parameters.relationship: SRTM 1 arc-second via Open Topo Data, bilinear, 60 m extension and 300 m backdrop, EGM96 heights; supplied-model terrain source and datum unrecorded.

parameters.name: Vista frame versus UTM
parameters.relationship: Vista's equirectangular frame about 49.2827 N, -123.1207 E differs from UTM 10N by about 5 m at 2.5 km and up to 34 m at its extent corners (computed).

parameters.name: Cone flip rate
parameters.relationship: Share of buildings whose intersection status with a cone changes after replacing OSM with LiDAR heights.

metrics.name: Share of buildings with measured height
metrics.good: 95% or more (LiDAR-derived)
metrics.basis: Vista baseline is 14.6% measured.

metrics.name: Median absolute difference versus published towers
metrics.good: 1 m or less
metrics.basis: Team tolerance aligned with 3D BAG 1.06 m median RMSE.

metrics.name: UBC bldgheight agreement
metrics.good: median absolute difference 1 m or less over 20 or more buildings
metrics.basis: UBC heights derive from 2021 LiDAR for LOD1 use.

metrics.name: SRTM-60 m minus City DTM on ground
metrics.good: absolute median 2 m or less, p95 5 m or less
metrics.basis: USGS actual SRTM error about 10 m; GLO-30 below 4 m LE90.

visualization: scatter LiDAR height versus Vista height
modules.limits: Published heights differ in definition (roof, architectural top). Wikipedia is a secondary source. No independent surveyed benchmarks were found for downtown roofs.

modules.name: Currency, provenance and licence manifest
modules.design_question: How are building currency, attribution and licence obligations tracked per layer so the open-source release stays compliant?
modules.method: Maintain layers.json with id, publisher, URL, retrieval date, upstream modified date, licence, required attribution text, CRS, vertical datum, edition (for example MRDEM 1.2), acquisition date and checksum. Generate in-app credits and README attribution from it. Flag buildings completed after 2022-09-09 (LiDAR acquisition) using published completion dates and an override table of published heights with citations (for example The Stack 2023, The Butterfly 2024). Keep ODbL (OSM) layers as a separate database from OGL-licensed City layers; do not merge OSM geometry into City-derived products without legal advice. Re-pull the view-cones dataset when its portal modified date changes (now 2026-10-19; Vista snapshot 2026-09-21). Include MRDEM's Copernicus WorldDEM credit text and OGL attribution statements. Ask the City whether combined-layer attribution wording is acceptable.

parameters.name: LiDAR currency cut-off
parameters.relationship: City 2022 LiDAR was acquired 7 and 9 Sept 2022; buildings completed later (The Stack 2023, The Butterfly 2024) get built_after_lidar = true.

parameters.name: ODbL isolation
parameters.relationship: Public use of an adapted OSM database requires offering that database under ODbL; keep OSM-derived tiles separate and labelled.

parameters.name: OGL-Vancouver attribution
parameters.relationship: Statement quoted by the OSM help forum: 'Contains information licensed under the Open Government Licence – Vancouver'; wording not confirmed on the City portal.

parameters.name: Re-pull trigger
parameters.relationship: View-cones modified 2026-10-19T13:35Z, after Vista's snapshot (portal_modified 2026-09-21); re-download and diff polygons.

metrics.name: Attribution completeness
metrics.good: 100% of shipped layers
metrics.basis: All licences found require attribution.

metrics.name: Stale-layer detection
metrics.good: upstream modified date compared at every build
metrics.basis: View-cones changed after Vista's snapshot.

metrics.name: Licence separation
metrics.good: OSM-derived tiles separate and labelled ODbL
metrics.basis: ODbL share-alike on adapted databases.

modules.limits: OGL-Vancouver full text was not readable; a 2011 commentary called it 'viral' and a 2017 forum thread left OSM compatibility unresolved. This is not legal advice.
modules.human_judgment: Obtain a licence opinion (course adviser or library) before mixing OSM and City data.

validation_cases.input: Tile 490000_5459000 SW corner lon -123.13750196, lat 49.28367088 into UTM 10N (GRS80, k0 0.9996, central meridian -123).
validation_cases.expected: E 490000.00, N 5459000.00; NE corner 491000.00, 5460000.00 (computed; confirm with pyproj EPSG:3157).

validation_cases.input: Vista anchor 49.2827 N, -123.1207 E into UTM 10N.
validation_cases.expected: E 491221.8, N 5458890.0, so tile 491000_5458000, which is one of the 13 City tiles within 2 km of downtown.

validation_cases.input: Vista model point (5674.2, -5083.1) m, inverted with its equirectangular formula, then to UTM 10N minus the anchor's UTM.
validation_cases.expected: Offset about (+5.8, -33.6) m, 34 m total; about 5 m at (2500, 0) (computed).

validation_cases.input: City 2009 rows for bldgid 149845 versus published 200.9 m (1128 W Georgia).
validation_cases.expected: 2009 shows topelev_m 223.71 over base about 30.8 m (2009 conditions). 2022 LiDAR roof max minus ground should be about 195 to 201 m; a gap above 3 m needs review.

validation_cases.input: Footprints of The Stack (2023) and The Butterfly (2024) versus LiDAR acquired 7 and 9 Sep 2022.
validation_cases.expected: LiDAR heights lower than published 162.3 m and 178.6 m, or absent; features flagged built_after_lidar.

validation_cases.input: CHS station 07735 offsets (CGVD2013 -2.88, CGVD28 -3.00) and PROJ vgridshift ca_nrc_HT2_2010v70_CGG2013a.tif at 49.2863, -123.0997.
validation_cases.expected: About +0.12 m higher in CGVD2013 if offsets are add-to-chart-datum values (convention unverified); the grid result should be within about 0.05 m.

validation_cases.input: 1040-1080 Barclay site-context lists 3.2.1 maximum geodetic elevation 123.201 m (12.1.1 is 121.695 m); sample City DTM at the site.
validation_cases.expected: h_allow = 123.201 minus Z_ground; compare with the document's own site grade (document not opened; value from a search summary).

validation_cases.input: 830-850 Thurlow / 1045 Haro staff presentation (2022-07-05) lists 3.2.1 at 361 ft; convert to metres.
validation_cases.expected: 361 ft = 110.03 m; if the cone is 123.201 m, ground is about 13.17 m, so the City DTM there should read about 13 m +/- 1 m (cone edition and datum unverified).

validation_cases.input: Sample MRDEM-30 DTM and the HRDEM DTM at 200 non-vegetated downtown points versus the City DTM after datum calibration.
validation_cases.expected: RMSE roughly 1.0 to 1.6 m and LE90 about 1.7 to 2.6 m, as in MRDEM spec Table 2 (1.04/1.69 versus RTK; 1.59/2.60 GLO-30-derived).

validation_cases.input: Run the pipeline on 20 or more UBC buildings; compare with ubcv_Structures bldgheight and baseelev.
validation_cases.expected: Median absolute height difference 1 m or less; base-elevation differences consistent with the datum offset.

validation_cases.input: Mount Seymour (49.39333, -122.94444) 1,449 m and Grouse Mountain 1,231 m (Wikipedia; datum unstated); sample each ring mesh.
validation_cases.expected: HRDEM and MRDEM within about 5 m; SRTM may be off by 10 to 20 m. Coarse check only.

validation_cases.input: d = 30,000 m, R = 6,371,000 m, refraction coefficient 0.13.
validation_cases.expected: d^2/(2R) = 70.6 m; with refraction 61.5 m (hand calculation).
About 30.9 m north-south by 20.1 m east-west, so Vista's 60 m sampling is coarser than the source (computed).

validation_cases.input: Synthetic 30 x 30 m flat roof at 150 m, 49 points per m2, Gaussian noise 0.08 m, plus wall points and 20 spikes.
validation_cases.expected: P90, P95 and max (after spike removal) within 0.3 m of 150 m, matching the 0.31 m flat-roof benchmark.

flags.claim: Google Open Buildings can supply Vancouver footprints.
flags.correction: Coverage is Africa, South and South-East Asia, Latin America and the Caribbean; Canada is not listed and the page names no height field.
flags.detail: Use City LiDAR, City 2015 footprints, OSM, Overture or Microsoft instead.

flags.claim: City building-footprint datasets carry height fields.
flags.correction: Only the 2009 set has elevations and heights, as roof-facet rows under 2009 conditions; 2015 and 1999 sets are geometry only.
flags.detail: 2009 rows near Shangri-La show a tower under construction; do not treat them as current.

flags.claim: The City publishes DEM or DSM products derived from 2018 and 2022 LiDAR.
flags.correction: 2018 and 2022 are zipped LAS tiles only; the only City raster DEM is the 2013 1 m GeoTIFF (1.91 GB).
flags.detail: We must derive DTM and DSM ourselves (M04).

flags.correction: 26910 is NAD83 (original); NAD83(CSRS) / UTM 10N is EPSG:3157. City LiDAR states NAD83(CSRS) 4.0.0.BC.1.GVRD.
flags.detail: EPSG remarks say sub-metre accuracy needs the CSRS code; City orthophotos are labelled EPSG:26910.

flags.claim: All elevation sources can be merged without datum work.
flags.correction: City LiDAR is CGVD28GVRD; HRDEM and MRDEM are CGVD2013; SRTM is EGM96; GLO-30 is EGM2008; OSM heights are relative.
flags.detail: CHS offsets imply about +0.12 m between CGVD2013 and CGVD28 (unverified); MRDEM v1.1 moved heights about 0.4 m.

flags.claim: Vista README: terrain is '60 m SRTM'.
flags.correction: SRTM 1 arc-second (about 30.9 x 20.1 m cells) sampled at 60 m (extension) and 300 m (backdrop), EGM96; supplied-model terrain source and datum are unrecorded.
flags.detail: Actual vertical error is about 10 m (USGS), unusable for cone height limits.

flags.claim: Vista's local equirectangular frame is adequate for cone tests.
flags.correction: It differs from UTM 10N by about 5 m at 2.5 km and up to 34 m at its extent corners (computed).
flags.detail: Fine for visuals; use UTM or a per-view ENU frame for geometry that touches cone edges.

flags.claim: Cone maximum geodetic heights are in CGVD28(GVRD).
flags.detail: LTSA 465C keeps CGVD28 as legal-survey datum and the Guidelines say 'maximum geodetic height' (s.2 p.3); the datum definition was not read (403). Ask views@vancouver.ca.

flags.claim: View 3.2.1 is 123.201 m geodetic (Barclay) and 361 ft at Thurlow.
flags.detail: Both PDFs were unopened (403); search summaries only. 3.2.1 was among views amended in 2024, so edition and datum may differ.

flags.claim: City OGL-Vancouver and OSM ODbL layers can be combined in one release.
flags.detail: A 2011 commentary called OGL-Vancouver 'viral'; a 2017 forum thread left compatibility open; ODbL has share-alike. Keep layers separate pending a legal opinion.

flags.claim: 2022 LiDAR is current for every downtown tower.
flags.correction: Acquisition was 7 and 9 Sept 2022; The Stack (2023) and The Butterfly (2024) post-date it.
flags.detail: Flag built_after_lidar and use a cited override table.

flags.claim: NRCan Automatically Extracted Buildings has usable heights for Vancouver.
flags.detail: Feature catalogue lists Height Maximum/Minimum, but a WMS GetFeatureInfo query downtown returned empty; coverage unconfirmed.

flags.claim: LidarBC datum and licence are known.
flags.detail: Catalogue gives no datum; license_title 'Access Only' conflicts with OGL-BC in the notes.

flags.claim: SRTM is adequate for 'as accurate as possible' North Shore mountains.
flags.correction: HRDEM (better than 1 m) and MRDEM-30 (about 1 to 2.6 m RMSE) are available over the same area; SRTM is about 10 m.
flags.detail: Slopes amplify horizontal error (20 m CE90 on 30 degrees gives 11.5 m vertical).

flags.claim: City LiDAR class names map to LAS codes 1 to 8.
flags.detail: The portal lists class names as a numbered list; ASPRS codes differ (for example water is 9, noise 7). Read the LAS header or a class histogram first.

flags.claim: HRDEM VILLE_VANCOUVER 2013 shares City LiDAR 2013's datum after conversion.
flags.detail: Source LiDAR is CGVD28; HRDEM claims CGVD2013; the STAC item has no vertical field. Check by sampling against the City DEM.

change_log: Round 1: first version of packet C02; no earlier version exists.
Corrected scope assumptions: Google Open Buildings has no Canada coverage; only the 2009 City footprints have heights; EPSG:26910 is not NAD83(CSRS); City publishes no 2018/2022 DEM rasters.
Added M01 datum registry after finding City LiDAR is CGVD28GVRD, HRDEM and MRDEM are CGVD2013, SRTM is EGM96, GLO-30 is EGM2008.
Added hand-checkable validation cases, including computed UTM tile corners and Vista-frame offsets.
notes: Recommended: City LiDAR 2022 (CGVD28GVRD) is the downtown source; HRDEM and MRDEM serve the mountains after datum calibration. Cone datum and 3.2.1 values remain unverified; confirm with views@vancouver.ca. Process LAS offline, ship only derived MB-scale files.
